evidence_basis: data/orders.db lookup on action.order_id (fixture cross-check, second independent path)
expected_evidence_state_rule: AVAILABLE when the record resolves; UNAVAILABLE when it does not (the downstream order-scoped facts cannot be obtained). Never CONTRADICTORY for this requirement — a missing row is an absence, not a conflicting value.
expected_requirement_state_rule: SATISFIED when action.order_id resolves to a row in the system of record; VIOLATED when a lookup runs and returns zero rows (a determinate negative); NOT_ESTABLISHED when the lookup could not run at all (typed SourceUnavailable). The P3-B corpus contains only the first two.
notes: DEGENERATE for measurement: the per-case requirement_state is a 1:1 recode of one corpus construction parameter (human_label_sample.csv record_lookup_status; extraction_gold_v1.meta.json counts.by_difficulty_class.record_unresolved_escalate = 4). Any aggregate coverage ratio over this requirement equals 1 - 4/30 = 0.8667 by construction and cannot fail for a reason not baked into how the 30 cases were sampled. This is the exact pattern docs/retired-figures.md item 2 retired ('the detector recomputed that same boolean from the same fields ... an identity, not a measurement'). The current runtime (decide.py + receipt.py) additionally CANNOT distinguish VIOLATED from NOT_ESTABLISHED: both a missing row and an unreadable source produce Confidence.NONE -> verdict SOURCE_UNRELIABLE, root_cause evidence_below_reliability_floor.

expected_requirement_state_rule: SATISFIED when action.currency equals the resolved order's currency column; VIOLATED when they differ (e.g. tool-call USD vs order INR); NOT_ESTABLISHED when the order record does not resolve. Every one of the 30 P3-B tool calls is INR and every one of the 109 rows in data/orders.db is INR, so no case can produce VIOLATED. P3-B marks it DORMANT for all 30. gold_set.jsonl gs-136..140 (currency=USD, orders resolve) would exercise it, but they are outside the frozen P3-B corpus. currency_integrity is also downstream of order_record_resolves (you cannot compare against an absent record).

rationale: currency_integrity is NOT structurally foundational. It is a value comparison between a structural tool-call field and a resolved order-record field — structurally identical to ORDER_ATTRIBUTES_MATCH (colour/category) and ORDER_BELONGS_TO_CUSTOMER (customer_id), both of which ARE ClaimKinds. It is 'unrepresentable' only because no ClaimKind was defined for it, not because it is a different kind of thing. P3-A's UNREPRESENTABLE_REQUIRED and P3-B's foundational_requirements[] both file it alongside order_record_resolves; the boundary test says that conflates two categories. P3-D section 21 already flags this ('does it get an evidence channel ... which would make it a representable claim and move it out of the foundational-requirement class entirely?').

expected_evidence_state_rule: AVAILABLE when the fields are present; UNAVAILABLE when a field is NULL; NOT_REQUIRED when the record is absent.
expected_requirement_state_rule: SATISFIED when the resolved row has non-NULL values for the load-bearing fields (customer_id, delivered_at, amount_paise, currency); VIOLATED when the row exists but a load-bearing field is NULL; NOT_APPLICABLE when the row does not resolve at all (subsumed by order_record_resolves).
notes: DEGENERATE: the frozen corpus has ZERO cases of a resolved-but-incomplete record. All 26 FOUND rows in data/orders.db have every load-bearing field populated (0 NULLs across all 109 rows). So this requirement contributes 26 identical SATISFIED observations with no discriminating power and 4 NOT_APPLICABLE — it is a pure denominator inflator on this corpus. The runtime cannot distinguish it from order_record_resolves anyway (orders.py returns Confidence.NONE for both).
